content.raw:
Monday’s Mississippi reports brought an active homicide investigation in Horn Lake, planned road closures in Lauderdale County and the death of a Tupelo High School football player. A Class 2A volleyball semifinal also offers a place in the state final. College reports cover soccer, tennis, basketball, volleyball and bowling. This edition draws on original articles published in the 24 hours ending at 4:45 p.m. Central on Monday, October 12; games scheduled after that cutoff are previews, not results.

Mississippi News

Horn Lake police investigate fatal restaurant shooting

Horn Lake police say 24-year-old Justin Conrad died after being shot at Kabuki restaurant on Goodman Road. His twin brother, Jaelind Conrad, was shot in the abdomen and was last reported in stable condition. A third man, 25-year-old Marterius McShane, was treated for a gunshot wound to the leg. Investigators say witness interviews and video led them to conclude McShane shot the brothers, and a murder warrant was issued in Justin Conrad’s death. Police said McShane was detained at a hospital pending medical release and custody on the warrant; an unidentified person also fired toward him as he left the scene. The investigation remains active. Read the MS News Group report.

Fisher Road closures planned Tuesday through Thursday

Lauderdale County Road and Bridge crews plan three cross-pipe replacements on Fisher Road, with closures to through traffic from 8 a.m. to 2 p.m. each day. Work is scheduled in the 5201–5257 block Tuesday, at 5754 Fisher Road Wednesday and at 5995 Fisher Road Thursday. Drivers should use an alternate route during the work. The county listed 601-482-9798 for questions. Read the MS News Group road notice.

Mississippi Sports

Tupelo mourns football player Alden Wade

Tupelo High School football player Alden Wade died in a single-vehicle crash early Sunday, according to Sports Mississippi. Tupelo police said officers responded to the 4900 block of Cliff Gookin Boulevard at about 1:11 a.m. and that accident reconstructionists were investigating. The police statement cited in the report did not identify the person who died; Sports Mississippi attributes the identification to a coroner’s account cited by another outlet. Head coach Ty Hardin and Tupelo High School issued tributes to Wade and support for his family, friends, teammates and classmates. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

East Union and Walnut meet with a state-final berth at stake

Unbeaten East Union, 36-0, hosts defending champion Walnut, 31-4, at 6 p.m. Monday in the Class 2A North Half volleyball championship. The winner advances to Thursday’s state final in Clinton. Sports Mississippi reports that Walnut took the first set of the teams’ September meeting, but East Union won the match and has swept 16 straight matches since. The rematch also carries an unusual milestone for Walnut: the school’s final season under its current name before consolidation with Falkner. The scheduled start was still ahead at this edition’s cutoff; no result is presumed. Read the Sports Mississippi matchup report.

Southern Miss soccer answers twice against Troy

Southern Miss women’s soccer twice came from behind to draw Troy 2-2 on Senior Day in Hattiesburg. Olivia Tribolet scored the equalizer in the 83rd minute, giving the Golden Eagles a Sun Belt Conference point. Sports Mississippi lists Southern Miss at 5-5-3 overall and 2-3-1 in league play after the match. The late goal kept a second deficit from becoming a home loss. Read the Sports Mississippi match report.

Ole Miss women receive preseason SEC recognition

SEC media projected Ole Miss women’s basketball to finish seventh among 16 conference teams, according to Sports Mississippi. Senior transfer Talaysia Cooper was named to the preseason All-SEC second team. These are preseason selections, not a result or final conference standing; they indicate how the team and Cooper were viewed before the season begins. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

Ole Miss doubles teams reach regional finals

Ole Miss reached doubles finals in separate ITA Southern Regional tennis events. In Auburn, Milburn and Igor Kudriashov won two Sunday matches to reach the men’s final scheduled for Monday. In Baton Rouge, Andrea Nova and Alice Soulie advanced to the women’s doubles final, while Alice Battesti reached a singles semifinal. The reports establish final berths, not championship results. Read the men’s report and the women’s report from Sports Mississippi.

William Carey rallies past Mississippi Valley State

William Carey women’s volleyball lost the opening set to Mississippi Valley State 25-19 on Sunday in Lorman, then won the next three 25-18, 25-19 and 25-17. The four-set comeback is the result reported by Sports Mississippi; its account does not provide individual player statistics. Read the Sports Mississippi match report.

Jackson State bowling finishes seventh

Jackson State finished seventh at the Colonial Lanes Classic in Louisiana. The Tigers went 2-1 in Sunday’s championship bracket, including a win over No. 20 UAB, according to Sports Mississippi. That ranked win was a notable result within the seventh-place finish; the brief report does not give a final pin total or full bracket path. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

Featured image: Southern Miss soccer file photo from the MS News Group media library, credited to Southern Miss Athletics. It does not depict the Troy match described here.

Sunday, October 11, 2026 — coverage originally published from 4:45 p.m. Saturday to 4:45 p.m. Sunday Central.

A 17-point comeback by Mississippi Valley State and a road win for Ole Miss headline a busy stretch of college sports reporting. Jackson State and Alcorn State also played Saturday football games, while Sunday brought new soccer and volleyball results. In Mississippi news, Prentiss County authorities are investigating the theft of a county work truck and other property. The summaries below draw on reports originally published during the 24-hour window ending at Sunday's 4:45 p.m. cutoff.

Mississippi News

Prentiss County shed burglary under investigation

The Prentiss County Sheriff's Office says someone entered the Supervisor District Shed at 283 County Road 8311 early Sunday and took vehicle batteries and other items. Authorities say the person then left in a white 2007 Ford F-150 four-door crew cab work truck belonging to a supervisor. The investigation is ongoing, and the department is asking people with information that could lead to an arrest to contact it or Crime Stoppers. The sheriff's account describes a suspect but does not report an arrest. Read the MS News Group report.

Mississippi Sports

Mississippi Valley State erases 17-point deficit

Mississippi Valley State came back from 17 points down to beat Texas Southern 38-34 in Houston on Saturday. Quarterback Josh Brown scored five touchdowns, according to the school account carried by Sports Mississippi. The size of the deficit and the narrow final margin make this one of the weekend's clearest Mississippi football turnarounds. The source report does not break down Brown's touchdowns or provide a play-by-play, so those details are not assumed here. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

Ole Miss wins at Vanderbilt

No. 9 Ole Miss won on the road at Vanderbilt in its second Southeastern Conference away game of the season. Sports Mississippi reports that the result moved the Rebels to 4-1 overall and 2-1 in SEC play. That conference record is the immediate consequence of the win; the available report does not give a final score or individual statistics. The result is included here without filling in those missing details from elsewhere. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

Jackson State loses a close game at Grambling State

No. 22 Jackson State fell 45-38 to Grambling State in Louisiana despite what Sports Mississippi describes as a career game by freshman Li'Darius Pryor. The seven-point margin shows how close the final result was, but the source does not provide Pryor's statistical line or describe the scoring sequence. This was a loss for Jackson State, even with the standout performance noted in the report. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

Alcorn State dominates its homecoming game

Alcorn State beat Arkansas Baptist 63-7 Saturday at its homecoming game. Sports Mississippi reports 323 rushing yards for the Braves and an attendance of 14,502 at Jack Spinks-Marino Casem Stadium. The account says Alcorn scored through offense and special teams, making this the widest margin among the four college football results in this edition. No individual scoring totals are provided in the available report. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

Jackson State soccer extends its SWAC run

Jackson State women's soccer beat Arkansas-Pine Bluff 6-0 Sunday at Pumphrey Stadium. The Tigers scored five times in the first half and once in the second, according to the school report carried by Sports Mississippi. It was Jackson State's fourth consecutive Southwestern Athletic Conference victory. The report does not identify the goal scorers, so the team result and conference streak are the clearest verified takeaways. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

Ole Miss volleyball pushes No. 4 Kentucky

Ole Miss lost 3-1 at No. 4 Kentucky on Sunday afternoon after taking one set from the Wildcats. The reported set scores were 25-22, 21-25, 25-19 and 25-21. The Rebels remained competitive across four sets but could not complete the road upset. The account attributes the match result to the school and says Kentucky extended its winning streak; it does not give a new Ole Miss record or player totals. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

Ole Miss rifle wins ranked tri-meet

The No. 5 Ole Miss rifle team won a home tri-meet Saturday with 4,724 points. No. 10 Memphis finished with 4,709 and No. 4 Nebraska with 4,696, according to Sports Mississippi. Ole Miss's margin was 15 points over Memphis and 28 over Nebraska. The result stands out because the Rebels finished ahead of two other ranked teams, including one ranked above them, though the short report offers no individual scores. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

Belhaven stays unbeaten in conference soccer

Abby Jordan scored in the 73rd minute to give Belhaven a 1-0 win over Asbury on Saturday at Belhaven Bowl Stadium. Goalkeeper Addi Roberts made four saves, and the Blazers recorded their sixth shutout of the season. Sports Mississippi reports that Belhaven remained unbeaten in CCS play. In a one-goal game, Jordan's late finish and Roberts's clean sheet supplied the decisive details in the available account. Read the Sports Mississippi report.

Featured image: MS News Group file photo of a football game. It is illustrative and does not depict the games reported above.
